title: Release version chip (v2.2.1) next to the logo and footer 'Version: 2.2.1' never render: provideReleaseVersion() is never registered
legacy: app/templates/partials/header.html.twig:35-39 renders v{{ app_version }} beside the brand (hidden < 400px, is-active on /changelog); app/templates/partials/footer.html.twig:82 renders 'footer.project.version' ("Version: 2.2.1") above 'Updated: 17/07/2026' in the Project column.
next: src/LoDb.Web/src/app/core/layout/header/header.html:22-32 and footer/footer.html:53-55 are gated on RELEASE_VERSION, whose default factory returns null (core/layout/shell/release-version.ts:8-11). The provider that feeds it, features/editorial/changelog/provide-release-version.ts:22-31 (provideReleaseVersion), is referenced nowhere (grep: only its definition), so neither app.config.ts:48-77 nor app.config.server.ts registers it. Result: no chip in the header at any width, no Version line in the footer, the chip is missing from the tab order (legacy tab #2).
evidence: shots/header-1440-old.png vs header-1440-new.png (chip absent), shots/footer-1440-old.png vs footer-1440-new.png (Project column has only 'Updated'); cmp/shots/home-1440-old.txt lines 'v2.2.1' and 'Version: 2.2.1' missing from home-1440-new.txt; curl /en/about and /en/: 0 occurrences of 'hx-version-chip'. Focus order legacy: brand, v2.2.1, HOME...; new: brand, HOME...
fix: 1) src/LoDb.Web/src/app/app.config.ts: add provideReleaseVersion() to providers (composition root, may import features; shared with app.config.server.ts via mergeApplicationConfig). 2) Make the build ship the manifest independently of the host checkout: in docker/next/web-ssr/Dockerfile, right after `COPY src/LoDb.Web/ ./`, add `RUN rm -rf src/app/features/editorial/changelog/published && ln -s ../../../../../../../app/public/changelog src/app/features/editorial/changelog/published` (the context already admits app/public/changelog/ and copies it to /source/app/public/changelog). Verify: curl -I http://localhost:18080/changelog/manifest.json -> 200; header chip 'v2.2.1' (visibility per Z01-07 matrix), footer Project column 'Version: 2.2.1' then 'Updated: 17/07/2026' (footer.html:53-56), chip aria-current + gold-bright border on /en/changelog, chip back in the tab order after the brand. The changelog page itself (Z08) is fixed by the same step 2.
verifyReason: Confirmed provideReleaseVersion() (features/editorial/changelog/provide-release-version.ts:22-31) is defined but never registered (grep: only its definition; commit b781abfe never touched app.config.ts, although its docblock says 'Registered in app.config.ts'). BUT registering it alone would still render nothing on the running stack: the lodb-next SSR image has no /app/browser/changelog (docker exec ls: absent), curl /changelog/manifest.json -> 404, and /en/changelog prints 'No release published yet' (shots/changelog-1440-new.txt). ChangelogReader.latestVersion() would resolve null. Cause: in this Windows checkout (git core.symlinks=false) src/app/features/editorial/changelog/published is not the committed relative symlink (git blob = '../../../../../../../app/public/changelog'); it is currently a junction to F:\...\app\public\changelog (readlink /f/Git/...), which resolves nowhere inside the Linux build container, so the angular.json asset glob copies nothing.

title: Header Encyclopedia links, footer site links and bottom-nav links drop the pinned patch (and the ?lang variant): they always jump back to the latest patch
legacy: All codex links are built with resource_path(route, {}, navVersion, navLang) (header.html.twig:57-68, footer.html.twig:31-38, bottom_nav.html.twig:264-296) using page_selection(); ResourceUrlGenerator.php:35-57 keeps /{version}/ in the path when it is not the latest and appends ?lang=. On /14.1.1/champions every Champions/Items/Runes/Summoners link points to /14.1.1/objects?lang=en_US etc.
next: header.ts:49-51, footer.ts:43-45 and bottom-nav.ts:20-22 all call localePath(locale, path) (core/layout/shell/locale-path.ts:8-10), which knows nothing of the version or the lang variant. On /en/14.1.1/champions the header, footer and bottom nav point to /en/champions, /en/items… (latest).
evidence: node shell.mjs links (zone dir): legacy /14.1.1/champions header=['/14.1.1/champions?lang=en_US','/14.1.1/objects?lang=en_US',...], bottom=['/', '/14.1.1/champions?lang=en_US', ...]; new /en/14.1.1/champions header/bottom/footer = ['/en/champions','/en/items','/en/runes','/en/summoners'].
fix: Add core/layout/shell/codex-context.ts exposing `injectCodexContext()`: a signal {version: string | null, lang: string | null} recomputed on NavigationEnd (toSignal with initialValue from router.routerState.snapshot) where version = params['version'] of the deepest ActivatedRouteSnapshot (only the `:version` mount of app.routes.ts:134-138 sets it; paramsInheritanceStrategy 'always' puts it on the leaf) and lang = queryParams['lang']. It needs no API, so it is correct on SSR and on prerendered pages (which never carry a version). Add a pure `codexPath(locale, version, path)` next to locale-path.ts returning `/${locale}/${version}/${path}` when version is set, else localePath(locale, path). Mark the four catalogue entries (`codex: true` on NavEntry) in site-links.ts and bottom-nav-entries.ts (CODEX_ENTRIES are all codex). In header.html (codex @for, lines 62-73), footer.html (site @for, lines 29-33) and bottom-nav.html (lines 2-8) bind codex entries with `[routerLink]="codexPath(...)"` and `[queryParams]="ctx().lang ? { lang: ctx().lang } : null"` (never a string holding '?', jalon 4 G3). Home, Trends, About, FAQ, Donate, API stay unversioned as in legacy. Let features/catalogue/shared/links/catalogue-href.ts reuse the same version-prefix rule instead of duplicating it. Add specs: header/bottom-nav on /en/14.1.1/champions point to /en/14.1.1/items etc. and keep ?lang=en_GB.
verifyReason: Confirmed: header.ts:49-51, footer.ts:43-45 (link()), bottom-nav.ts:20-22 all use localePath(locale, path); curl /en/14.1.1/champions lists only /en/champions, /en/items, /en/runes, /en/summoners in the chrome (x3 each) while legacy resource_path keeps /14.1.1/ (ResourceUrlGenerator.php:35-57). Not an intentional divergence (ADR 0005 only says path > query > cookie). The auditor's implementation is more complex than needed: the version is already a router param, so no /api/meta matcher and no UrlTree/string parsing are required.

title: A facet group folds itself under the pointer when its last facet is cleared
legacy: FacetPanel.vue:39-66: a `folded` map remembers the reader's folding; a watcher pins any group that becomes engaged to open, so 'clearing the last facet of a group must not fold it under the pointer'.
next: facet-panel.ts:49-56 recomputes `isOpen = isGroupOpenByDefault(group, facets)` on every state change and binds it to `[expanded]`: engaging a Ratings range flips it to true, clearing it flips it back to false and the CDK item collapses.

fix: In facet-panel.ts, add `private readonly folded = signal<Record<string, boolean>>({})`. `groups` computes `isOpen: folded()[group.name] ?? isGroupOpenByDefault(group, facets)`. An `effect()` runs over groupFacets(offered) and, for every group with countEngaged > 0 and no entry in folded(), sets it to true, since an engagement pins the group open. The facet-group (toggled) handler writes `folded.update(f => ({...f, [name]: !isOpen}))`. To keep the sheet's folding across reopenings, like the legacy, hold that map in CatalogueFilter as `foldedBy: Record<'rail'|'sheet', Record<string, boolean>>` signals, and give FacetPanel a `surface = input<'rail'|'sheet'>('rail')` (filter-sheet.html passes `surface="sheet"`). Rail and sheet stay independent. Add a spec: engage then clear a range, and the group stays expanded.
verifyReason: Confirmed from the code: facet-panel.ts:49-56 recomputes isOpen from isGroupOpenByDefault and binds it to [expanded], so clearing the last facet flips the binding to false and the CDK item folds. Legacy FacetPanel.vue:39-66 keeps a `folded` map and pins engaged groups open. There is a second, related divergence. The legacy sheet is mounted once (Teleport to body, showModal/close), so its folding survives closing and reopening the sheet. The new CDK sheet builds a fresh FacetPanel on every open, so the reader's folding resets each time.

title: Noxus theme: the crimson hoist bar on every plate (stats card, lore, tips, skin tiles) is gone
legacy: app/assets/styles/theme/noxus/frames.css:24 sets `border-left: 3px solid var(--color-hex-deep)`, giving a crimson rgb(192,32,58) bar down the start edge of each hextech-frame (the stats aside, the lore and tips cards). The hover rule at :39 sets it to `--color-hex`.
next: src/LoDb.Web/src/styles/theme/noxus/frames.css:21-34 declares `border-color: color-mix(...)` and then `border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--color-hex-deep)`. The build emits an `@supports (color: color-mix(in lab, red, red)) { [data-theme="noxus"] .hextech-frame { border-color: color-mix(...) } }` fallback AFTER the rule, so the shorthand repaints the inline-start side steel grey. The 3px width stays; the crimson is lost. The hover rule at :38-45 has the same problem.
evidence: out/theme-noxus-old.png (red bar on the stats aside) vs out/theme-noxus-new.png (grey bar). Computed border-left-color on #stats frame and #lore frame: old rgb(192, 32, 58); new color(srgb 0.227 0.267 0.282 / 0.7). --color-hex-deep is #c0203a in both. The rule list captured on the page shows the trailing @supports block.
fix: In styles/theme/noxus/frames.css, remove `border-inline-start` from the rule at :21-34 and add, right after it, a separate `[data-theme='noxus'] .hextech-frame { border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--color-hex-deep); }`. Remove `border-inline-start-color` from the hover rule at :38-45 and add a separate `[data-theme='noxus'] .hextech-frame-hover:hover { border-inline-start-color: var(--color-hex); }` after it. An equivalent fix: move the colour-mix into a Noxus token (`--nx-plate-edge: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-blue-steel) 70%, transparent)` on `[data-theme='noxus']`) and write `border-color: var(--nx-plate-edge)`; no fallback then follows the rule. Afterwards, check that the computed border-left-color on `#stats` and on the lore frame is rgb(192, 32, 58) in the Noxus theme.
verifyReason: The served bundle /build/styles-MI2QP67Y.css contains `[data-theme=noxus] .hextech-frame{…border-color:color-mix(in srgb,#005a82 70%,transparent);border-inline-start:3px solid var(--color-hex-deep)…}` followed by `@supports (color: color-mix(in lab,red,red)){[data-theme=noxus] .hextech-frame{border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--color-blue-steel) 70%,transparent)}}`, which repaints the start side. The hover rule has the same problem. That fallback is emitted by Tailwind 4.3.3 (@tailwindcss/postcss). I checked the proposed fix by compiling a test file with the repo's @tailwindcss/postcss and minify on: a separate later rule holding only `border-inline-start` is emitted after the @supports block, and so is a rule whose border-color is a custom property. Both keep the crimson side. The same mechanism breaks `.hx-toast`: `border:1px solid color-mix(...)` is re-emitted in @supports after `border-inline-start:2px solid currentColor`, which loses the coloured start bar. That is outside this zone and belongs to the design-system zone.

Verify Back walks the fragments, the URL stays correct, and each heading lands below the chips.

Native fragment navigation (location.hash) is tracked cleanly by the Router, and Back walks #lore, #skins, the page, then the list (out/back3.json). next: src/LoDb.Web/src/app/app.config.ts:58 enables anchorScrolling. Angular's ViewportScroller.scrollToAnchor ignores scroll-margin (offset [0,0]), so the card lands at top 0 by click or direct load. The scroll-mt-24 (6rem) on rune-constellation.html:11,46 has no effect and differs from the legacy 5.5rem.

fix: Add a browser-only environment initializer in src/LoDb.Web/src/app/core/routing/ (e.g. provide-anchor-offset.ts, registered in app.config.ts next to withInMemoryScrolling). It calls inject(ViewportScroller).setOffset(() => { const id = decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)); const target = id ? document.getElementById(id) : null; return [0, target ? parseFloat(getComputedStyle(target).scrollMarginBlockStart) || 0 : 0]; }), which mirrors native fragment scrolling. Then remove scroll-mt-24 from rune-constellation.html:11 and :46, so the global [id] 5.5rem of styles/foundation/base.css:72 applies (legacy lands the card 88px below the top).
verifyReason: The Angular 22.2 source confirms the gap: BrowserViewportScroller.scrollToElement (node_modules/@angular/common/fesm2022/common.mjs:156-166) scrolls to rect.top minus a fixed offset and ignores scroll-margin. The global setOffset proposed first would force one value on every anchor, but the legacy uses 5.5rem for [id] and 6.5rem for .hx-prose section (prose.css:13, new prose.css:11). The offset should read the target's own scroll margin instead.

title: Changelog is empty: the release files never reach the build (symlink checked out as a plain file)
legacy: app/templates/changelog/index.html.twig:30-39 renders the 19 releases read server-side from app/public/changelog/*.json (timeline, latest open, hero 'Current version v2.2.1' :24-27, codex meta 'v2.2.1' :17). The same version feeds the navbar chip and the footer 'Version: 2.2.1'.

RELEASE_VERSION (provide-release-version.ts) stays null, so the header chip v2.2.1 and footer 'Version' line disappear site-wide too.
evidence: shots/changelog-1440-new.png shows only the hero + 'No release published yet.' vs shots/changelog-1440-old.png (19 releases). `docker exec lodb-next-web-ssr-1 ls browser/changelog` -> No such file; `curl localhost:18080/changelog/manifest.json` -> 404; `git ls-files -s .../changelog/published` -> 120000, `git config core.symlinks` -> false. With the JSON injected by Playwright route interception (zones/Z08/cl.mjs, changelog-inj-1440-new.png / -390-new.png) the new timeline is text-identical to legacy (diff of innerText empty) and visually matches: only the data feed is broken.
fix: docker/next/web-ssr/Dockerfile, between `COPY src/LoDb.Web/ ./` and the build: `RUN rm -rf src/app/features/editorial/changelog/published && ln -s /source/app/public/changelog src/app/features/editorial/changelog/published`. /source/app/public/changelog is already copied at line 12, so the link resolves whatever the host checkout holds (text file, junction or real symlink). Then make the build fail on a missing feed: `RUN npm run build:web && test -f dist/web/browser/changelog/manifest.json`. Keep angular.json unchanged (the input must stay inside the workspace). Add a line to docs/guides/dev-next.md: on Windows, local `ng serve` needs `git config core.symlinks true` (Developer Mode) or a junction. Rebuild lodb-next-web-ssr and check /en/changelog (19 releases, the latest open), the 'Current version v2.2.1' plate, the codex meta, the header chip and the footer 'Version: 2.2.1' line.
verifyReason: Confirmed on the running stack: /en/changelog shows only the hero and 'No release published yet.', `curl :18080/changelog/manifest.json` is 404 and the container has no browser/changelog (lodb-next-web-ssr-1 was restarted, not rebuilt). `published` is mode 120000 in git and core.symlinks=false. Note: someone replaced it in this checkout with a Windows junction at 12:05 today; BuildKit would copy that as a symlink to an absolute F:\ path, which is broken inside the container, so the Dockerfile fix is still needed. With the JSON injected the timeline matches legacy, in en, fr and ar. One part of the auditor's fix is wrong: pointing the angular.json asset `input` at `../../app/public/changelog` is refused by @angular/build (normalize-asset-patterns.js: 'The … asset path must be within the workspace root.'). That is why a symlink exists at all. `ln -sfn` over a directory that has already been copied is also fragile.

next: Route headings 'nav.profile' and 'profile.preview.badge' (src/LoDb.Web/src/app/features/account/account.routes.ts:28-33) -> 'My profile · League of Data Base', 'Preview · League of Data Base'.
evidence: TITLE lines of shots/profileF-1440-{old,new}.txt and previewF-1440-{old,new}.txt.
fix: Add an AccountHead service (features/account/shared/account-head.ts) provided by AccountPage, holding `override = signal<{ text: string } | { key: string } | null>(null)`. AccountPage calls applyPrivateHead with a computed that prefers the override: extend applyPrivateHead to accept `Signal<{ key: string } | { text: string }>`, translating only `key`. ProfileEditor and ProfilePreview set `{ text: displayName(...) }` once the profile is loaded (profile-editor.ts name() already computes it), and reset it to null on destroy. The route key stays the fallback before loading.
verifyReason: The titles are confirmed: 'ParityAudit · League of Data Base' vs 'My profile · …', and 'ParityAudit — League Of Data Base' vs 'Preview · …'. The fix needs a correction. AccountPage writes the head for every account view (account-page.ts:40, applyPrivateHead from route data). A second applyPrivateHead in ProfileEditor or ProfilePreview would race it: two effects, each calling seo.apply asynchronously. applyPrivateHead also translates its input as a key, so a raw display name would go through transloco.translate as a missing key.

title: Key creation date and usage days rendered as locale short dates ('9/27/26') instead of dd/mm/yyyy

fix: (1) Never let a render with a missing catalogue be stored. In src/LoDb.Web/src/app/core/i18n/loading/transloco-http-loader.ts, pipe getTranslation through catchError, which on the server (isPlatformServer) calls inject(PageResponse).cache('private') and then rethrows. Transloco keeps its fallback behaviour, but nginx no longer caches that HTML. Do the same in the `.catch` of core/i18n/activate-locale.ts:42 (the root catalogue). Make sure no later resolver overrides it: resolveCatalogueContext calls response.cache() before the render starts, so a failure raised during the render wins. (2) Optional, and it removes the failure mode: provide, in app.config.server.ts only, a server TranslocoLoader that reads dist/browser/i18n/<path>.json from disk once per process (memoized Map) instead of self-HTTP. It must also write each catalogue into TransferState under the same key the browser loader reads, or the browser downloads the catalogues again. (3) Extend core/i18n/loading/ssr-catalogues.spec.ts: when the stubbed fetch rejects a scoped catalogue, the rendered response carries Cache-Control 'private, no-store'. Not in this zone: the web-ssr heap exhaustion that triggers these failures belongs to infra/Z01. Z12-11 also removes this particular key from the summoners page.
verifyReason: The symptom is real, but the proposed cause and fix (1) are not. Evidence of the symptom: when I checked, nginx still held STALE copies of /pt/summoners and /th/summoners with placeholder="summoners.search_placeholder" (Date 10:52, cache-control latest). They revalidated to translated HTML afterwards. There is no render race. Direct renders on the SSR (:18082), 168 of them (21 locales x 8 scoped pages, concurrency 3 and 6), all came back translated (skeptic/probe.mjs). The HttpClient load a pipe starts is already awaited by the render through PendingTasks. So a route resolver that pre-loads scopes (fix 1) changes nothing. Raw keys appear only when the self-origin catalogue fetch fails. `docker logs lodb-next-web-ssr-1` shows 'FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit … JavaScript heap out of memory', RestartCount=3, and 503s at the time of the auditor's burst. A failed scope load is swallowed, and the render still goes out as a cacheable 200: s-maxage=300 + swr=3600 for latest, 604800 (7 days) for archived pages. The legacy (Twig, server-side trans with fallback) could never ship a raw key.

page: Return visits, / and pages without context
title: The choice is kept only when "Remember me" is ticked, and never for the UI language: / falls back to Accept-Language
legacy: HomeController.php:28-35 and :86-88: every switch writes the signed preference cookie for 30 days ("Remember me" widens it to 365) plus the session. ClientManager.php:74-91 reads it on every request, so the next visit to any URL, / included, opens in the chosen UI language and patch.
next: context-switcher.ts:135 stores lod_prefs only when the box is ticked (preferencesOf), and Preferences (core/context/preferences/preferences.ts, PREFERENCES_FIELDS = {lang, version}) holds no locale. src/server.ts:55-58 answers / from Accept-Language only. A French browser that switched to English lands on /fr/ next time. A variant or patch chosen without ticking the box is lost at the first header click (Z12-03).
evidence: curl -D - / with Accept-Language fr → Location: /fr/, de → /de/, none → /en/ (no cookie input possible). preferences-cookie-entry.ts:6 has a fixed 365-day lifetime and forgets when unticked.
fix: (a) Session memory, legacy parity without a cookie: in features/context-switcher/context-switcher.ts apply(), always write the chosen {locale, lang, version} to sessionStorage (key 'lodb.context', inside try/catch) through a new core/context/preferences/session-choice.ts. followRemembered (context-switcher.ts:158-168) and the NavContext of Z12-03 read it before the lod_prefs cookie, through the same rememberedTarget rules. (b) Remembered locale: add `locale: Locale | null` to core/context/preferences/preferences.ts and `locale: 'loc'` to preferences-fields.ts. Write and parse it in preferences-cookie-entry.ts and preferences-from-cookie.ts, validated against LOCALES. preferencesOf sets it from target.locale, so remembering the locale's own language and the latest patch is no longer an empty cookie. Keep the remember-only rule and the lifetime. (c) '/': in docker/next/nginx/sites/site.conf, add at http level `map $cookie_lod_prefs $lodb_pref_locale { default ""; "~(^|&)loc=(?<l>ar|cs|de|el|en|es|fr|hu|id|it|ja|ko|pl|pt|ro|ru|th|tr|vi|zh-hans|zh-hant)(&|$)" $l; }`. In `location = /`, add `if ($lodb_pref_locale != "") { add_header Cache-Control "private, no-store" always; return 302 /$lodb_pref_locale/; }` before proxy_pass. Otherwise the SSR's Accept-Language negotiation stays. (d) Update the lod_prefs row of the cookie policy (see Z12-M02).
verifyReason: The legacy behaviour is as described in code: HomeController.php:28-35, the preferenceCookie at 30 or 365 days, and the session at :86-88. But writing lod_prefs on every apply would contradict the published cookie policy. Both stacks show the same row: 'Preference (set only if you tick "remember"…)' (app/templates/legal/en/cookies.html.twig:51-56, features/editorial/legal/texts/cookies-en.html:40-46). The legacy code contradicted its own legal text, so the new remember-only cookie is the compliant behaviour. The real player-facing gaps are two. (1) Without 'remember', the legacy kept the switcher choice for the whole browsing session: clean URLs render the session patch (PageContextResolver.php:196-204), and the nav carries it. The new forgets it at the first link that does not carry it. (2) Remembering the locale is impossible. preferencesOf (selection/preferences-of.ts) keeps only lang (variants) and version, so a French browser that ticks 'remember' on English/latest writes {lang:null, version:null}. preferencesCookieEntry then expires the cookie (value '' → max-age 0), and '/' 302s to /fr/ from Accept-Language (server.ts:55-58). ADR 0005 ('Priorité : chemin > query > cookie, pour chaque axe (locale, version)') supports honouring a remembered locale, as long as the SSR itself reads no cookie.

page: Lists and trends in id, ja, ko, th, vi, zh-hans, zh-hant
title: The English fallback reads "1 results" / "Show 1 results" in locales whose plural rules have only "other"
legacy: components/codex/list_filter.html.twig:19-20 passes results and resultsOne, and the island picks the _one message when the count is 1, so every locale shows "1 result" (the en fallback for ja…).
next: filter.results and filter.show_results are ICU plurals that exist only in en/fr (public/i18n/en.json). In id/ja/ko/th/vi/zh they fall back to en but are compiled with the active locale's CLDR rules (core/i18n/provide-i18n.ts:27-29, strictPluralKeys:false), which have no `one` → "1 results".
evidence: zone one.mjs: /ja|ko|zh-hans/champions?q=ahri toolbar "1 results"; en "1 result", fr "1 résultat". Trends ja: zone shots/ja-trends-1440-new.txt "1 RESULTS".
fix: In src/LoDb.Web/public/i18n/en.json, change filter.results to `{count, plural, =1 {# result} other {# results}}` and filter.show_results to `{count, plural, =1 {Show # result} other {Show # results}}`. fr.json keeps its `one` form, which fr's rules cover. Add a case to core/i18n/provide-i18n.spec.ts: active lang 'ja', key only in en, count 1 → '1 result'. Translating these two keys into the 7 locales is an optional improvement, since the legacy had none.
verifyReason: Confirmed. shots/ja-trends-1440-new.txt:18 reads '1 RESULTS'. public/i18n/en.json:204/:218 are `one`-based ICU plurals. provide-i18n.ts:25-27 compiles fallback en messages with the active locale's CLDR rules, which have no `one` in id/ja/ko/th/vi/zh, so `other` is picked. The legacy fell back to the English '%count% result' through its _one key. The fix can be simpler and closer to the legacy: an exact `=1` selector matches whatever the locale's plural rules, so the English fallback reads '1 result' again in every locale. No new translations are needed. These are the only two root plural messages (admin is pinned to fr).

title: On a shared build, picking another language in the switcher does nothing
legacy: On /b/9e4e1c33acae52a5968d66a7, picking Français and submitting posts /setup-submit (HomeController.php:67-95). It redirects to /b/…?lang=fr_FR&version=16.19.1 with html lang=fr, chip '16.19.1 · FR', data and chrome in French ('Épée des Darkin', 'ORDRE D'ACHAT') and the 'Preferences saved' toast.
next: On /b/708073019671104ebabe9da0, picking 'fr:fr_FR' and submitting leaves the URL unchanged, html lang=en, chip '16.19.1 · EN', everything in English. targetOf (features/context-switcher/selection/target-of.ts) gives {locale:'fr', lang:null}. switchContext (core/context/switch/switch-context.ts:46-50) sets locale=null because current.locale is null, and lang=variantOf(null)=null. The rewritten URL equals the current one, so navigateByUrl is a no-op. The share route supports ?lang= (share.routes.ts doc): /b/…?lang=fr_FR renders 'Épée des Darkin' but keeps the chrome in English (html lang=en, 'Purchase order'). currentChoice (selection/current-choice.ts:31-36) also ignores ?lang= there and shows English.
evidence: zone skeptic/share.mjs vs skeptic/share-old.mjs, before/after output quoted above. curl /b/708073019671104ebabe9da0?lang=fr_FR: <html lang="en">, 1x 'Épée des Darkin', 3x 'Purchase order'.
fix: (1) In src/LoDb.Web/src/app/core/context/switch/switch-context.ts, when current.locale === null, the language cannot ride the path. Set lang to `target.lang ?? (target.locale ? languageOf(meta, target.locale) : kept(undefined, current.query.get('lang')))`, keep it in ?lang=, and skip variantOf. Add cases to its spec for /b/{token} → /b/{token}?lang=fr_FR. (2) In features/context-switcher/selection/current-choice.ts, on a page without a locale, select the option whose `language` equals ?lang= across all options. (3) For chrome parity, add core/i18n/activate-locale-from-lang.ts, a ResolveFn that maps ?lang= to the locale whose meta.locales language shares its primary subtag (fr_FR→fr, en_GB→en), falling back to DEFAULT_LOCALE, and then does what activateLocale does. Attach it to the ':token' route of features/builds/share/share.routes.ts, with runGuardsAndResolvers already on query change. This reads no cookie, so ADR 0005 holds, and the page stays noindex.

The legacy cookie was indeed signed and HttpOnly (ClientManager::makeRememberCookie).
next: features/editorial/legal/texts/cookies-en.html:40-46 and cookies-fr.html carry the same text. The new cookie is different: core/context/preferences/preferences-cookie.ts:5 ('unsigned and readable by scripts') and preferences-cookie-entry.ts:6,27-31 (max-age 365 days, no HttpOnly, Secure only on https). The page the switcher's 'Remember me' relies on now misstates the cookie's nature and lifetime. It also constrains Z12-09.
evidence: grep lod_prefs: src/LoDb.Web/src/app/features/editorial/legal/texts/cookies-en.html:40, cookies-fr.html:40, and the code above.
fix: Rewrite the lod_prefs row in src/LoDb.Web/src/app/features/editorial/legal/texts/cookies-en.html:40-46 and cookies-fr.html:40-46. Alternatively, lower ONE_YEAR_IN_SECONDS in preferences-cookie-entry.ts to the announced 7 days. Either way the policy and the code must agree. Mention the added `loc` field if Z12-09 is applied. Legal wording is the owner's call.
